## Purpose

This procedure describes the setup, operation, routine maintenance,
and troubleshooting of the Hach DR3900 benchtop spectrophotometer as a
laboratory instrument. The DR3900 uses a tungsten lamp (visible range)
and a deuterium lamp (UV range) to measure absorbance and transmittance
across 320--1100 nm, supporting both factory-stored programs for Hach
reagent kits and user-defined wavelength methods
[@hach_dr3900; @hach_water_analysis2024].

For method-specific chemistry, reagent handling, and the analyte Method
Registry (nutrients, metals, and general water quality parameters), see
[SOP-L303 Hach Colorimetric Analysis](SOP-L303-hach-colorimetric.qmd).
For field use of the portable Hach DR900 colorimeter, see
[SOP-F208 Portable Spectrophotometer / Colorimeter (Field)](../field_sops/SOP-F208-portable-colorimeter-field.qmd).


## Scope

- **Applies to:** All use of the Hach DR3900 benchtop spectrophotometer
  in the EA Program laboratory, including stored-program colorimetric
  analysis, user-defined single-wavelength measurements, wavelength
  scans, and time-course (kinetic) measurements
- **Does not apply to:** Micro-volume UV-Vis measurements (see
  [SOP-L212 NanoDrop](SOP-L212-nanodrop-spectrophotometer.qmd));
  fluorometric quantification (see
  [SOP-L203 Trilogy Fluorometer](SOP-L203-trilogy-fluorometer.qmd));
  portable field colorimetry (see
  [SOP-F208](../field_sops/SOP-F208-portable-colorimeter-field.qmd));
  general spectrophotometer theory (see
  [SOP-L201](SOP-TBD.qmd))
- **Location:** EA Program laboratory, SGM 133

## Definitions

- **Absorbance (A):** The negative base-10 logarithm of transmittance: $A = -\log_{10}(T)$; directly proportional to analyte concentration (Beer-Lambert law) within the linear range of the instrument.
- **Beer-Lambert law:** The relationship between absorbance, path length, and concentration: $A = \varepsilon \cdot c \cdot l$, where $\varepsilon$ is the molar absorptivity, $c$ is concentration, and $l$ is the optical path length (cell width); the basis for all colorimetric quantification.
- **Blank (reagent blank):** A sample containing all reagents except the analyte; used to zero the instrument and correct for absorbance contributed by the reagent matrix.
- **Colorimetric method:** An analytical technique in which a chemical reagent reacts with the analyte to produce a colored complex whose absorbance is proportional to analyte concentration.
- **TNT plus vial:** A Hach proprietary pre-dosed reagent vial for the DR3900; contains all required reagents sealed in a glass vial; provides consistent results without manual reagent preparation.
- **Transmittance (T):** The fraction of incident light that passes through the sample: $T = I/I_0$; related to absorbance by $A = -\log_{10}(T)$.
- **Wavelength scan:** A measurement mode in which the instrument records absorbance across a range of wavelengths to identify the absorption maximum of an unknown compound.


## Safety and Hazards

::: {.callout-warning}
### Hazards

- **Optical:** The deuterium lamp emits ultraviolet radiation. Do not
  look directly into the sample compartment when the lid is open and the
  lamp is on. The instrument's interlock dims the lamp when the lid is
  raised, but UV exposure remains possible during diagnostic modes.
- **Chemical:** Sample solutions and reagents placed in the instrument
  may be hazardous. Refer to the relevant method SOP (e.g.,
  [SOP-L303](SOP-L303-hach-colorimetric.qmd)) and the reagent SDS for
  handling precautions.
- **Electrical:** Do not operate the instrument with wet hands or near
  standing water. If liquid enters the instrument housing, disconnect
  power immediately and contact the lab manager.
:::

### Required PPE

- [ ] Safety glasses
- [ ] Lab coat
- [ ] Nitrile gloves (when handling reagents or samples)

### Emergency Procedures

For chemical spills on or near the instrument, clean the spill per
[SOP-L003 Hazardous Materials Handling](SOP-L003-hazardous-materials-handling.qmd)
before resuming use. If liquid enters the instrument, unplug the power
cord and do not attempt to power on until the lab manager has inspected
the unit.


## Equipment and Materials

### Equipment

| Item                              | Location         | Notes                          |
|:----------------------------------|:-----------------|:-------------------------------|
| Hach DR3900 benchtop spectrophotometer | Lab bench, SGM 133 | Wavelength range 320--1100 nm |
| Light shield / adapter            | With DR3900      | For 13 mm and 16 mm round vials (TNT plus) |
| USB cable or Ethernet connection  | Lab bench        | For data export to PC          |

### Sample Cells

| Cell Type                     | Path Length | Use                                |
|:------------------------------|:-----------|:-----------------------------------|
| 10 mm square glass or quartz  | 10 mm      | General absorbance; user-defined methods |
| 1-inch round glass            | 25.4 mm    | Most Hach stored-program methods   |
| 16 mm round (TNT plus vials)  | 16 mm      | TNT plus pre-dosed vial methods    |

### Consumables

| Item                          | Notes                                     |
|:------------------------------|:------------------------------------------|
| Lint-free wipes (Kimwipes)    | For cleaning sample cell exteriors         |
| Silicone oil and applicator cloth | For 1-inch round cells (reduces light scattering at the glass surface) |
| DI water (Type II or better)  | For blanking and rinsing                   |


## Procedure

### Startup and Self-Check

1. Verify that the sample compartment is empty and the lid is closed
2. Turn on the DR3900 using the power switch on the rear panel
3. The instrument performs an automatic self-check, including lamp
   tests and wavelength verification. This takes approximately 30
   seconds. Do not open the lid or insert samples until the home screen
   appears.
4. Allow the lamps to warm up for at least 15 minutes before making
   measurements that require high photometric accuracy (e.g.,
   user-defined methods at low absorbance). For routine stored-program
   analyses, measurements may begin after the self-check completes.

### Selecting an Operating Mode

From the home screen, select one of the following modes:

| Mode                  | When to Use                                    |
|:----------------------|:-----------------------------------------------|
| **Stored Programs**   | Pre-programmed Hach reagent kit methods; see [SOP-L303](SOP-L303-hach-colorimetric.qmd) for the Method Registry |
| **Single Wavelength** | User-defined absorbance or %T at a specific wavelength |
| **Multi Wavelength**  | Simultaneous measurement at 2--4 wavelengths   |
| **Wavelength Scan**   | Absorbance spectrum over a defined range       |
| **Time Course**       | Kinetic measurement at a fixed wavelength over time |

### Preparing and Inserting Sample Cells

1. **Select the correct cell type** for the method (see Section 5).
   Square cells must be oriented so the clear optical faces align with
   the light path (arrow on the cell pointing toward the detector).
2. **Fill the cell** to the level required by the method. Do not
   overfill; liquid on the outside of the cell causes erroneous
   readings.
3. **Clean the exterior** of the cell with a lint-free wipe. For
   1-inch round cells, apply a thin film of silicone oil and wipe with
   the oiling cloth to eliminate fingerprints and water droplets
   [@hach_dr3900].
4. **Insert the cell** into the cell holder. Close the sample
   compartment lid fully before reading.

::: {.callout-tip}
### Cuvette Selection for UV Work
Standard glass and plastic cells absorb UV light below approximately
340 nm. For measurements below 340 nm in user-defined or wavelength
scan modes, use quartz cells [@skoog2018].
:::

### Zeroing (Blanking) the Instrument

1. Fill a clean cell with the blank solution. The blank must match the
   sample matrix: DI water for simple aqueous samples, or the reagent
   blank specified by the Hach method.
2. Insert the blank cell and close the lid
3. Press **Zero** (stored-program mode) or **Zero/Blank** (single
   wavelength mode)
4. Verify that the display reads 0.000 Abs (or 100.0 %T)
5. Remove the blank cell

::: {.callout-note}
Re-zero whenever you change wavelengths, switch cell types, or if the
instrument has been idle for more than 30 minutes.
:::

### Measuring Samples

1. Insert the sample cell and close the lid
2. Press **Read** (or **Measure** in scan/time-course modes)
3. Record the result (absorbance, concentration, or %T depending on
   mode)
4. Remove the cell. Rinse and refill for the next sample, or use a
   fresh cell.

### Wavelength Scan Mode

1. From the home screen, select **Wavelength Scan**
2. Set the start and end wavelengths and the scan increment (typically
   1 nm)
3. Zero the instrument with a blank across the full scan range
4. Insert the sample and press **Start Scan**
5. The spectrum is displayed on screen. Use the cursor to read peak
   wavelengths and absorbance values.
6. Export the scan data via USB (see Section 6.8)

### User-Defined Programs

The DR3900 allows creation of custom calibration curves for analytes
not covered by the factory-stored programs:

1. Select **User Programs** from the home screen, then **New**
2. Set the measurement wavelength, units, and cell type
3. Prepare a series of standards spanning the expected concentration
   range (minimum 5 points plus a blank)
4. Read each standard and enter the known concentration when prompted
5. The instrument fits a calibration curve (linear, polynomial, or
   segmented). Review the correlation coefficient ($r^2$); accept only
   if $r^2 \geq 0.995$ for linear methods [@harris2020].
6. Save the program with a descriptive name and program number

### Data Export

1. Connect a USB flash drive to the USB-A port on the front panel
2. From the home screen, select **Data Log**
3. Select the readings to export and press **Send to USB**
4. Data are saved as `.csv` files that can be opened in R or Excel
5. Alternatively, connect the DR3900 to a PC via USB cable and use
   Hach's LINK2SC or Claros software for direct data transfer

### Shutdown

1. Remove all cells from the sample compartment
2. Wipe the cell holder with a dry lint-free tissue to remove any
   spilled liquid
3. Close the sample compartment lid
4. Turn off the instrument using the rear power switch
5. Cover the instrument with the dust cover if one is available


## Quality Control and Acceptance Criteria

### Daily Verification

Before each analytical session:

- Run a DI water blank; the reading should be 0.000 $\pm$ 0.005 Abs
  at the working wavelength
- Run a Hach-supplied verification standard (e.g., StablCal formazin
  standard or NIST-traceable absorbance filter) at the working
  wavelength. Acceptance: within $\pm$ 0.01 Abs of the certified
  value, or $\pm$ 5%, whichever is larger.

### Lamp Monitoring

The DR3900 tracks lamp hours internally. When a lamp approaches its
rated lifetime (typically 2000 hours for deuterium, longer for
tungsten), the instrument displays a warning.

- Record lamp hours monthly in the instrument log
- Replace lamps per the Hach service manual or contact Hach technical
  support
- After lamp replacement, run the full wavelength verification
  procedure

### Annual Verification

At least once per year (or after any service event):

1. Run a multi-wavelength check using a NIST-traceable holmium oxide
   filter to verify wavelength accuracy ($\pm$ 1 nm)
2. Run a multi-point photometric accuracy check using neutral density
   filters or potassium dichromate standards across the range
   0.1--1.5 Abs [@skoog2018]
3. Record results in the instrument log and retain the verification
   report


## Troubleshooting

| Symptom                              | Possible Cause                     | Action                              |
|:-------------------------------------|:-----------------------------------|:------------------------------------|
| Self-check fails                     | Lamp failure or firmware error     | Note the error code; contact lab manager |
| Blank does not zero                  | Dirty cell, wrong cell type, or stale blank | Clean or replace cell; prepare fresh blank |
| Erratic readings                     | Air bubbles in cell, condensation, or dirty optics | Degas sample; wipe cell; clean sample compartment |
| "Lamp intensity low" warning         | Lamp nearing end of life           | Schedule lamp replacement           |
| Readings drift over time             | Lamp not warmed up; temperature change | Allow 15 min warm-up; avoid drafts near instrument |
| Absorbance exceeds 2.5               | Sample too concentrated            | Dilute sample and re-read           |


## Waste Disposal

| Waste Type                    | Disposal Method                          |
|:------------------------------|:-----------------------------------------|
| Rinsate from cells (DI water) | Drain                                    |
| Chemical samples / reagent waste | Per method SOP (see [SOP-L303](SOP-L303-hach-colorimetric.qmd)) |
| Used lint-free wipes          | Standard trash unless contaminated       |
| Spent lamps                   | Hazardous waste (deuterium lamps contain UV-emitting gas); dispose through EH&S |

## Training Record

Before operating the DR3900 independently, personnel must:

1. Read this SOP in full
2. Complete [SOP-L002 Laboratory Safety](SOP-L002-laboratory-safety.qmd)
   training
3. Read [SOP-L303](SOP-L303-hach-colorimetric.qmd) if performing
   colorimetric analyses
4. Observe a trained operator perform a complete session: startup,
   self-check, zeroing, sample measurement, data export, and shutdown
5. Perform a supervised session with acceptable QC results (blank
   within specification, verification standard within tolerance)
6. Be signed off by the PI or lab manager
